To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
school system leaders' educational infrastructure building activities were motivated by and in pursuit of both institutional ritual and technical efficiency.

(a) the U.S. institutional environment has changed over a quarter century, with a shift from a focus on equalizing access to education to one of improving educational quality; (b) U.S. educational systems are responding to this change in the institutional environment by developing educational infrastructures that are intended to couple their formal organizations with the new institutional environment; and (c) these educational infrastructure building processes can be motivated by, or in pursuit of, both ritual and technical rationalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how school system leaders make sense of their environments and how they attempt to manage their organizations in the context of this sense making.
how system leaders make sense of and act on the changing institutional environment of U. S. school systems in an effort to build systems capable of improving instruction.
the ways in which school systems are attempting to build educational systems in a changed institutional environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the educational infrastructure building efforts of school systems are simultaneously motivated by, and are in pursuit of, ritual and technical rationalities.
the school systems' educational system infrastructure building efforts were simultaneously ritual and instrumental in nature.
educational infrastructure building is an institutionalized effort to build a system that can be more effective in influencing instruction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

school systems' infrastructure building efforts are intended to improve the quality of instruction, yet these efforts are also motivated by a concern to legitimate and rationalize the system's organization in a changing educational environment.
the U.S. educational sector has changed considerably and the educational system building efforts of system leaders are intended to manage these changes in the institutional environment.
the U.S. educational system is being built to improve instruction by coupling formal organizational elements with environmental cues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
school systems' sense making about and efforts to build educational infrastructure to improve instruction are complex and multifaceted.

system leaders in a standards and test based environment are attempting to build educational systems by coupling their formal organization with the environmental cues they notice and interpret in their efforts to influence classroom instruction, and these efforts are simultaneously motivated by, and pursuing, both institutional ritual and technical efficiency.
the institutional environment is a critical factor in understanding how school systems attempt to build their educational systems.
